Ultralytics creates cutting-edge, state-of-the-art (SOTA) YOLO models built on years of foundational research in computer vision and AI. Constantly updated for performance and flexibility, our models are fast, accurate, and easy to use. They excel at object detection, instance segmentation, semantic segmentation, depth estimation, image classification, pose estimation, and oriented object detection tasks, and can track detected objects across video frames.

Find detailed documentation in the Ultralytics Docs. Get support via GitHub Issues. Join discussions on Discord, Reddit, and the Ultralytics Community Forums!

Request an Enterprise License for commercial use at Ultralytics Licensing.

📄 Documentation

See below for quickstart installation and usage examples. For comprehensive guidance on training, validation, prediction, and deployment, refer to our full Ultralytics Docs.

Install

Install the ultralytics package, including all requirements, in a Python>=3.8 environment with PyTorch>=1.8.

pip install ultralytics

For alternative installation methods, including Conda, Docker, and building from source via Git, please consult the Quickstart Guide.

Usage

CLI

You can use Ultralytics YOLO directly from the Command Line Interface (CLI) with the yolo command:

# Predict using a pretrained YOLO model (e.g., YOLO26n) on an image
yolo predict model=yolo26n.pt source='https://ultralytics.com/images/bus.jpg'

The yolo command supports various tasks and modes, accepting additional arguments like imgsz=640. Explore the YOLO CLI Docs for more examples.

Python

Ultralytics YOLO can also be integrated directly into your Python projects. It accepts the same configuration arguments as the CLI:

from ultralytics import YOLO

# Load a pretrained YOLO26n model
model = YOLO("yolo26n.pt")

# Train the model on the COCO8 dataset for 100 epochs
train_results = model.train(
    data="coco8.yaml",  # Path to dataset configuration file
    epochs=100,  # Number of training epochs
    imgsz=640,  # Image size for training
    device="cpu",  # Device to run on (e.g., 'cpu', 0, [0,1,2,3])
)

# Evaluate the model's performance on the validation set
metrics = model.val()

# Perform object detection on an image
results = model("path/to/image.jpg")  # Predict on an image
results[0].show()  # Display results

# Export the model to ONNX format for deployment
path = model.export(format="onnx")  # Returns the path to the exported model

Discover more examples in the YOLO Python Docs.

✨ Models

YOLO27 — Coming Soon: Preview the upcoming family, currently undergoing final R&D. Models are not yet available, and no launch date is set.

Ultralytics supports a wide range of YOLO models, from early versions like YOLOv3 to the latest YOLO26. The tables below showcase YOLO26 models pretrained on COCO for Detection, Segmentation, and Pose Estimation. Semantic Segmentation models are pretrained on Cityscapes, Depth Estimation models are pretrained on a broad multi-dataset mix and evaluated on NYU Depth V2, Classification models are pretrained on ImageNet, and OBB models are pretrained on DOTAv1. Tracking mode is compatible with Detection, Segmentation, Pose, and OBB models. The listed pretrained models download automatically from the latest Ultralytics release on first use.

releases.name: v8.4.218 - `ultralytics 8.4.218` Stop `yolo` commands crashing when sentry-sdk 3 is installed (#27341)
releases.body:
## 🌟 Summary
Ultralytics 8.4.218 fixes `yolo` commands crashing when Sentry SDK 3 is installed.

## 📊 Key Changes
- 🔧 Updated Sentry configuration to use Sentry SDK 3’s replacement setting, while keeping the existing option for older Sentry versions.
- 🚫 Continues to disable collecting local variables in stack frames.

## 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- ✅ Restores `yolo` commands, including prediction, for users with Sentry SDK 3 installed.
- 🏗️ Fixes the same issue affecting Ultralytics Platform worker image builds.
- ℹ️ This is a compatibility fix; it does not change models or prediction behavior.

## What's Changed
* `ultralytics 8.4.218` Stop `yolo` commands crashing when sentry-sdk 3 is installed by @glenn-jocher in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/27341


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/compare/v8.4.217...v8.4.218

releases.name: v8.4.217 - `ultralytics 8.4.217` More accurate TensorRT INT8 exports (#27340)
releases.body:
## 🌟 Summary
Release **8.4.217** improves TensorRT INT8 export accuracy and adds more flexible high-resolution tiling, alongside inference, validation, and export fixes.

## 📊 Key Changes
- 🎯 **More accurate TensorRT 11 INT8 exports:** Calibration now uses ModelOpt’s `entropy` method instead of `max`. With 128 calibration images, accuracy improved on every tested model—by up to **30 mAP50-95 points for pose**, **20 for segmentation**, **1.9 for OBB**, and **0.9 for detection**.
- 🧩 **More flexible tiling:** Training, validation, and prediction now support rectangular tile sizes and a configurable overlap, helping users process large images with more control.
- ⚙️ **Improved runtime and export support:** CoreML predictions are faster on image folders and videos; ExecuTorch inference now works with `device="mps"`; and YOLO26 Axelera exports select the accurate head when `nms=True`.
- 🛠️ **Reliability and metric fixes:** Corrects `single_cls` mAP calculations, prevents custom paths containing “lvis” from being mistaken for LVIS, makes detection summaries JSON-friendly, and preserves prediction frames when saving frames without a video.

releases.name: v8.4.216 - `ultralytics 8.4.216` ST Edge AI export for STM32 devices (#27291)
releases.body:
## 🌟 Summary
**Ultralytics 8.4.216 adds export support for STM32 edge devices and improves training, inference reliability, and deployment guidance across the ecosystem.**

## 📊 Key Changes
- **STM32 export with ST Edge AI:** The new `format="stedgeai"` export creates ONNX models for ST Edge AI Core and STM32 devices, including STM32N6. It supports float and INT8 export, with normalized detection and keypoint coordinates to support whole-graph quantization. This is the release’s main feature and also enables Ultralytics Platform to offer the format.
- **Better training behavior on AMD GPUs:** ROCm training now keeps the NCHW layout by default, avoiding a layout that was substantially slower on some Radeon hardware. AMD GPU metrics are also reported during ROCm training.
- **More reliable model use and exports:** Fixes include support for YOLOE prompts and TorchScript with PyTorch 2.16, correct CPU handling for `device="cpu:0"`, and restored top-1 accuracy for INT8 LiteRT and NXP classification exports.
- **Fixes for validation, masks, and video:** Validation now keeps separate per-image metrics for same-named files in different folders and handles mixed relative and absolute path

releases.name: v8.4.215 - `ultralytics 8.4.215` Plot, convert and prompt segmentation masks without the dense mask stack (#27216)
releases.body:
## 🌟 Summary
**YOLO 8.4.215 improves segmentation memory efficiency and fixes several data, tracking, and reliability issues—without changing model architectures or default prediction settings.**

## 📊 Key Changes
- 🧠 **Lower-memory segmentation workflows (main release change):** Plotting, saving, displaying, moving, and prompting segmentation masks can now work with masks stored inside their bounding boxes instead of building a full image-sized mask stack. Outputs and defaults remain unchanged; requesting `masks.data` still creates the dense masks.
- 🏷️ **More reliable automatic annotations:** Class labels stay matched to their detections when SAM filters out some masks.
- 🎥 **More complete video predictions:** Video loading now reads frames until decoding ends, rather than stopping at a possibly inaccurate frame count in the file metadata.
- 🧭 **More dependable tracking fallback:** If ECC camera-motion estimation fails, the tracker now retains the identity transform instead of potentially using a partially modified estimate.

releases.name: v8.4.214 - Read every image upright: apply EXIF orientation for all formats and flags (#27168)
releases.body:
## 🌟 Summary
**v8.4.214 makes image orientation consistent across reads**, helping ensure labels, predictions, and displayed images all use the same upright view. It also includes platform, hardware-compatibility, and reliability fixes, plus a substantially refreshed OpenVINO guide.

## 📊 Key Changes
- 🖼️ **EXIF orientation is now applied consistently when reading images**, across supported formats, read flags, and OpenCV versions. This is the release’s main functional change: images should appear in the same orientation that viewers display, reducing the risk of labels or predictions being rotated relative to the image.
- 📚 **OpenVINO documentation was reorganized and expanded** with clearer export and deployment steps, INT8 quantization guidance, device behavior and limitations, and updated benchmarks for YOLO26 on server CPUs and Intel Core Ultra hardware. The guide documents deployment options rather than introducing a new model.
- 🧠 **Segmentation mask shape checks avoid building full mask arrays** when only the shape is requested, reducing unnecessary memory use.
- 🖥️ **GPU detection now uses PyTorch’s device list**, allowing AMD GPUs to be detected even when NVIDIA too

aiSummary.oneLiner: The official framework for YOLOv8, offering state-of-the-art object detection and image segmentation.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: This repository contains the Ultralytics framework, the official home of the highly acclaimed YOLO (You Only Look Once) vision models, specifically YOLOv8. It provides a comprehensive suite for training, validating, and deploying state-of-the-art computer vision models. The framework simplifies complex tasks like object detection, instance segmentation, and image classification into an accessible, unified API. It is heavily optimized for inference speed and accuracy, making it suitable for real-time applications on edge devices. The project includes extensive documentation and tools for dataset management and model exporting to various formats.
keyFeatures: Unified API: Offers a single, consistent interface for detection, segmentation, and classification tasks.
High performance: Delivers cutting-edge accuracy and inference speeds suitable for real-time video analysis.
Broad export support: Easily exports models to formats like ONNX, TensorRT, and CoreML for diverse deployment.
Built-in dataset tools: Provides utilities to automatically format and validate common vision datasets.
Pre-trained models: Includes a vast library of highly accurate models pre-trained on the COCO dataset.
